episodes.title: Boolean algebra & K-maps
episodes.description: Describe logic gates, simplify Boolean expressions and group truth-table rows using Karnaugh maps.
topics: Why digital logic uses two states
NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR and literals
Choose large groups and permit overlap
Essential prime implicants and minimum covers

chapters.title: Why digital logic uses two states
NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR and literals
Choose large groups and permit overlap
Essential prime implicants and minimum covers

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome back. Maya here, with Leo. We've reached the section called Boolean algebra & K-maps.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Learn the rule. Build the circuit. Make it stick.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: describe logic gates, simplify Boolean expressions and group truth-table rows using Karnaugh maps.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with why digital logic uses two states and work our way to positive and negative logic conventions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Can you walk me through why digital logic uses two states?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Digital logic models signals using two values, 0 and 1. A truth table lists every allowed input combination and the output produced for it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: AND means output 1 only when every input is 1. OR: output 1 when any input is 1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Think of two switches A and B. If a lamp needs both switches on, its rule is F=AB.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For inputs 00, 01, 10, 11, the outputs are 0, 0, 0, 1. Boolean 1+1 is 1 because + means OR, not integer addition.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: OR is Boolean disjunction, not ordinary integer addition.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to boolean operations and circuits. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Use NOT, AND, and OR to build expressions. Series switches model AND; parallel switches model OR. A truth table evaluates every possible input assignment.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: NOT 0 equals what?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Complement swaps the two Boolean values: NOT zero is one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Binary uses only digits 0 and 1. Moving left doubles a digit’s weight; the rightmost integer position has weight 1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Base or radix means number of digit symbols in a numeral system.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: To convert 22 back, divide repeatedly by 2 and read the remainders from last to first.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Convert decimal values by choosing the largest remaining binary weight first. For example, 600 equals 512 + 64 + 16 + 8. Powers of two and all-one patterns make conversion faster.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: After removing 512 from 600, what remains?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Subtract the largest selected weight: 600 - 512 = 88.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR and literals to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A Boolean identity replaces an expression with an equivalent one. Equivalence means the output agrees for every input combination.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Literal means a variable or its complement, such as A or A′.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Simplify A+AB by factoring: A(1+B). Because 1 OR B is always 1, this becomes A·1=A.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You can verify it by testing both values of A; when A=0 both terms vanish, and when A=1 the output is already 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A Boolean function maps each binary input assignment to one output. Prove identities by considering input cases or comparing truth tables. Complement and algebraic laws provide equivalent ways to describe a function.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Product means AND of literals. Sum: OR of terms.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How many input assignments for a function of two variables?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The domain has the four rows 00, 01, 10, 11.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 4.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A complement reverses a function’s output. A dual is formed by exchanging AND/OR and 0/1 without changing the literals.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: De Morgan means (AB)′=A′+B′ and (A+B)′=A′B′.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For F=A+B, its complement is A′B′, while its dual is AB.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: At A=0,B=0, the complement is 1 but the dual is 0, so these operations are different.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The same bits can represent different values under different signed or coding conventions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We also need to talk about simplify and justify.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Simplification reduces an expression without changing its output on any input. Try factoring, absorption or checking the cases of one variable.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Absorption means A+AB=A and A(A+B)=A.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Simplify AB + ABC.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: AB absorbs ABC because whenever ABC is one, AB already is one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Canonical expressions use one term for each selected truth-table row. The variable order determines the binary row index.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Minterm means an AND term true on exactly one row; every variable appears once.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: With variable order A,B,C, index 5 is binary 101. Its minterm is AB′C, true only at 101.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Its maxterm is A′+B+C′, false only at 101. A function’s SOP selects its one rows; canonical POS selects its zero rows.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A minterm is one on exactly one row. A maxterm is zero on exactly one row. Their literal polarities depend on the explicitly stated variable order.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Maxterm means an OR term false on exactly one row.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Order A,B,C: minterm for 010?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Each literal must equal one at input 010.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose A'BC'.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: properties of canonical terms.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Corresponding minterms and maxterms select the same input row with opposite output values. Use their complement relationship to move between one-row and zero-row descriptions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How many rows make m2 AND m5 equal one?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two different minterms demand different full assignments, so their AND is zero.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Canonical SOP uses true minterms; canonical POS uses false maxterms. Both represent the same function. They are equivalent descriptions rather than dual functions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Canonical SOP for A OR B?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: OR is one on indices 1, 2, and 3.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with sum m(1,2,3).

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A sum of products (SOP), also called disjunctive normal form (DNF), joins AND terms with OR. A product of sums (POS), also called conjunctive normal form (CNF), joins OR terms with AND. Minterm indices identify input rows where the function is one. Combining functions with OR takes a union; AND takes an intersection.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Canonical DNF is...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Canonical SOP uses complete minterms.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us Sum of minterms.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack convert POS and complement safely next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Convert a POS expression by finding its false maxterms directly, or by complementing it into SOP and taking the remaining row indices. Both methods must produce the same truth table.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Two variables: zeros of (A+B)(A+B')?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The first factor is zero at 00, the second at 01; the expression simplifies to A.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 0 and 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A Karnaugh map (K-map) arranges rows so neighbors differ in one variable. Grouping allows the changing variables to disappear from a product term.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For variables A,B,C, rows 100 and 101 differ only in C. Their terms AB′C′ + AB′C combine to AB′(C′+C)=AB′.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Diagonal contact alone does not make two map cells adjacent.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Power-of-two cubes eliminate changing variables. Larger valid groups yield shorter product terms. Cover all required ones; overlapping groups are allowed.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four variables: an eight-cell cube leaves how many literals?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An eight-cell cube eliminates three variables, leaving one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with four-variable maps and POS minimization. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Four-variable K-maps use Gray-order numbering. Minimize SOP by grouping ones into product terms; minimize POS by grouping zeros into sum terms.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: At row AB=01, column CD=11, what minterm index belongs there?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: ABCD is 0111, binary seven.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us 7.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A dont-care is an unspecified output, not a mandatory one. Use it only when it improves a grouping. Prime implicants are valid cubes that cannot be enlarged.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: In SOP, a dont-care may be treated as...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Its output is unspecified, so either assignment is acceptable.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose One or zero as useful.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An implicant is a product term that never covers a required zero. A prime implicant is a valid group that cannot be enlarged; an essential one uniquely covers a required one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Cover means a collection of groups including every required one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Suppose one required cell is covered only by group P, while another is covered by P or Q. P is mandatory.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: After choosing P, mark everything it covers before selecting groups for any remaining uncovered cells.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on dual functions and self-duality.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A dual exchanges AND with OR and 0 with 1. From a truth table, evaluate it by complementing the inputs, reading the original output, then complementing that output.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Self-dual means the dual function equals the original on every row.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Three variables: input index 2 has complementary index what?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The complementary index is 2^3 - 1 - 2 = 5.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two-input XOR is one when its inputs differ. In a chain of XOR operations, equal pairs cancel and the result is one if an odd number of inputs are one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: 1 XOR 0 XOR 1 gives 0 because the two ones cancel. Three ones give 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For (1 XNOR 0) XNOR 1, the first stage gives 0 and the second also gives 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A circuit has physical low and high signal levels. A chosen convention assigns those levels the Boolean labels 0 and 1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Positive logic means high means 1 and low means 0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: In negative logic, logical one is the...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Negative logic reverses the positive assignment of physical levels.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose Low level.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave boolean algebra & K-maps, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Digital logic models signals using two values, 0 and 1. A truth table lists every allowed input combination and the output produced for it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A circuit has physical low and high signal levels. A chosen convention assigns those levels the Boolean labels 0 and 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: When you try a problem on positive and negative logic conventions, talk through why each step works. That's a useful check on what has clicked.

episodes.title: Number systems & codes
episodes.description: Convert number bases, encode signed values and distinguish binary, BCD and Gray codes.
topics: Group bits into octal and hex
Add signed values in different systems
Extend signed values without changing them
Compute Gray using a shift and XOR

chapters.title: Group bits into octal and hex
Add signed values in different systems
Extend signed values without changing them
Compute Gray using a shift and XOR

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I'm Maya, and this is CSQuest Audio. Today, Leo and I are taking on Number systems & codes.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Learn the rule. Build the circuit. Make it stick.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: convert number bases, encode signed values and distinguish binary, BCD and Gray codes.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with radix, octal, hex and fractions and work our way to compute Gray using a shift and XOR.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to radix, octal, hex and fractions. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: In base r, integer positions have weights 1,r,r² and fractional positions have weights 1/r,1/r². The digit symbols must fit the chosen base.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Hex 2A equals 2×16+10=42, and corresponds to binary 0010 1010. Binary 0.101 equals 1/2+1/8=0.625.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Group binary digits outward from the radix point when converting to octal or hex.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: group bits into octal and hex.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Bases eight and sixteen provide convenient binary shorthand. Group integer bits from the radix point leftwards and fractional bits from the radix point rightwards.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Binary 101101 as an octal numeral: enter its digits.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Group the bits into 101 followed by 101. Each triple is octal five, giving the octal numeral 55.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Binary addition uses positional arithmetic, not Boolean OR. Add the input bits and incoming carry in each column.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Add binary 11 and 01. The right column totals two, so write 0 and carry 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The next column totals 1+0+1=2, so write 0 and carry 1 again. The result is 100, which is decimal 4.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Choose the base and digit width first. Replacing a subtracted value by its complement converts subtraction into addition with a defined carry rule.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Three-digit decimal nines complement of 246?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: At three decimal digits, subtract from 999: 999 - 246 = 753.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack practice radix-complement subtraction next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Radix-complement subtraction requires aligned operand widths and correct final-carry handling. Pad operands before taking a complement, and interpret a negative result in the same representation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: With two decimal digits, subtract 23 from 50 using the tens complement 100−23=77. Add 50+77=127 and discard the final carry to get 27.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Using the nines complement 76 instead gives 126; add the carry to retained 26 to obtain 27.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Unlike radix-complement subtraction, r-minus-one complement subtraction uses an end-around carry. Add the carry to the retained low digits to restore the correct difference.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit ones complement of unsigned 3: unsigned value?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 1111 minus 0011 is 1100, unsigned twelve.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 12.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A bit pattern is not inherently positive or negative. A signed encoding defines how its leading bit and remaining bits represent a value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Sign magnitude means leading sign bit plus an unsigned magnitude.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: In four bits, +3 is 0011. Sign magnitude represents −3 as 1011, ones complement as 1100 and twos complement as 1101.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The same pattern can mean different values under different encodings.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with ranges and zero representations. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Signed ranges follow from the available bit patterns and zero representations. Sign-magnitude and ones complement use two zero patterns; twos complement has one extra negative value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ones complement means invert every bit of a positive pattern to encode its negative.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Minimum four-bit sign-magnitude value?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Three magnitude bits hold at most seven, so the minimum is negative seven.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with -7.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Binary arithmetic works column by column. The width and signed representation decide what to do with an extra carry and whether the mathematical result fits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Unsigned n-bit range means 0 through 2^n−1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit twos-complement 0011 + 1110 represents 3+(−2). The raw sum is 10001; retain 0001, which is +1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Overflow is a separate range question, not simply the existence of that discarded carry.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Ones-complement encoding forms a negative value by flipping every bit of its positive magnitude; twos complement also adds one. These encodings use different carry-handling rules. Preserve the representation across encoding, arithmetic, and final interpretation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Twos-complement n-bit range means −2^(n−1) through 2^(n−1)−1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit ones complement: encode -2 as its unsigned pattern value.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Positive two is 0010; invert to 1101, unsigned thirteen.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 13.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The same bits can represent different values under different signed or coding conventions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on define overflow using the representation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Overflow means the true arithmetic result is outside the range of the chosen representation. The same stored bits can overflow as signed arithmetic and remain valid as unsigned arithmetic, or vice versa.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit unsigned 9+6 overflows?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The sum fifteen is within the unsigned range zero through fifteen.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is No.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Sign tests and carry comparisons detect signed overflow. For twos-complement addition, overflow is carry into the sign bit XOR carry out of it. Other encodings require their own arithmetic rules.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit twos-complement 7+3 gives stored 1010. Overflow?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Both operands are positive but the retained signed sum is negative.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with Yes.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Extension adds bit positions while preserving the represented number. The correct padding depends on the encoding.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Unsigned means add leading zeros.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit twos-complement −3 is 1101; widening to eight bits gives 11111101. Four-bit unsigned 1101 is 13 instead and widens to 00001101.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Identical original bits require different padding under different interpretations.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Now for binary codes and minimum width. What's the key distinction?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A code assigns a bit pattern to a symbol or decimal digit. Its pattern need not equal that symbol’s ordinary positional binary value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: BCD means binary-coded decimal, encoding each decimal digit separately in four bits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Can two different messages share one codeword in an unambiguous fixed-length code?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The receiver needs each codeword to identify exactly one message.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose No.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Digit-wise BCD differs from whole-number binary. Weighted codes assign positional weights; ASCII assigns codes to characters. Excess-three is a self-complementary decimal code.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Excess-3 means encode a decimal digit after adding three.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Decimal 25 is BCD 0010 0101 because its digits are 2 and 5. Ordinary binary 25 is 11001.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For excess-three, add three to decimal digit two to obtain decimal five, whose four-bit code is 0101.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Reflected Gray code orders bit patterns so adjacent code words differ at one bit. Gray positions are not ordinary binary place values.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Binary to Gray means keep the top bit; XOR each lower binary bit with its left neighbor.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How many bit positions change from binary 0111 to 1000?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Ordinary binary counting changes all four positions at that boundary.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 4.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to compute Gray using a shift and XOR. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Convert an unsigned binary value to reflected Gray by XOR with itself shifted right by one bit. Hamming distance measures the number of differing bit positions between codewords.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Gray to binary means keep the top bit; each lower binary bit is previous binary bit XOR current Gray bit.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Binary 101 converts to Gray 111: keep 1, then 1 XOR 0=1 and 0 XOR 1=1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Decode 111 back by cumulative XOR to obtain 101.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave number systems & codes, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: In base r, integer positions have weights 1,r,r² and fractional positions have weights 1/r,1/r². The digit symbols must fit the chosen base.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Convert an unsigned binary value to reflected Gray by XOR with itself shifted right by one bit. Hamming distance measures the number of differing bit positions between codewords.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Take a small example of radix, octal, hex and fractions and work it out before looking at the explanation. Then compare your reasoning.

episodes.title: Combinational building blocks
episodes.description: Build selection and routing functions with multiplexers, decoders and encoders.
topics: Realize Boolean functions with a mux
Mux practice: choose the right cofactors
How small a mux can realize a function?
Build large muxes from smaller muxes

chapters.title: Realize Boolean functions with a mux
Mux practice: choose the right cofactors
How small a mux can realize a function?
Build large muxes from smaller muxes

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Maya and Leo here. Our section today is Combinational building blocks.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Learn the rule. Build the circuit. Make it stick.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: build selection and routing functions with multiplexers, decoders and encoders.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with compact truth tables and cofactors and work our way to realize Boolean functions with decoders.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: compact truth tables and cofactors.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A compact truth table can store a smaller function for each selector combination. Reconstruct the full output by choosing the matching case.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Selector means input bits deciding which case applies.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: If selector A chooses F0=B when A=0 and F1=B′ when A=1, then F=A′B+AB′.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: To fill a full truth table, evaluate the chosen case separately for each value of the remaining input.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on multiplexers select one data input.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A multiplexer (mux) routes one of several input values to a single output. Its select bits encode which input is chosen.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I0 is chosen by selector 0; I1 by selector 1 in a 2 means 1 mux.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A 4-to-1 multiplexer needs how many select lines?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two bits encode the four indices zero through three.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 2.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A selector chooses a route; it is not the data being routed.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Realize Boolean functions by assigning constants and remaining variables to mux data pins. Select a variable, compute its two cofactors, and connect them to the zero and one branches.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Enable means a control that permits operation; check whether it is active-high or active-low.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For a 2:1 mux with selector A, I0=B and I1=B′, the output is B when A=0 and B′ when A=1. This realizes XOR: F=A′B+AB′.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A 4:1 mux uses two selectors and four data inputs.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Truth tables, canonical row sets, and compact tables determine mux data inputs. Work in the stated selector order and distinguish remaining input functions from constants.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: XOR realized using a 4-to-1 mux and constants needs which data column?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: XOR is one precisely when A,B differ.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 0,1,1,0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Can you walk me through how small a mux can realize a function?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Using all variables as selectors permits constant data pins. Leaving one variable on data pins gives a smaller mux that may need an inverter. State which signals and extra gates are available.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A three-variable function realized using only truth-table constants needs how many mux data pins?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: All three variables are selectors, giving 2^3 = 8 branches.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Mux trees combine smaller selectors into a larger selector. Count components separately from serial stages. Low-order bits select within a group; high-order bits select the group.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How many 2-to-1 muxes build a complete 4-to-1 mux tree?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two leaf selectors plus one final selector give three components.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 3.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An enable input controls whether normal mux selection is permitted. In an AND-gated mux, the disabled output is zero. Active-high and active-low conventions specify the level that enables operation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The enable pin controls...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Enable gates the operation; select pins choose the route.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is Whether normal mux operation is permitted.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to demultiplexers distribute one input. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A decoder activates a line selected by a binary code. An encoder performs the opposite kind of conversion. A demultiplexer routes a data value to a selected output.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: One-hot means exactly one input line is active.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A 1-to-8 demux has how many data inputs?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The single input D is routed to one of the eight possible destinations.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An ordinary binary encoder reports the index of one active input and assumes exactly one request is high. Its simple OR equations do not resolve simultaneous requests as a priority encoder would.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Priority encoder means a stated ordering chooses a winner when several requests are active.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An enabled active-high 2-to-4 decoder given address 10 asserts output Y2: Y3Y2Y1Y0=0100. An active-low version asserts that same line with a zero: 1011.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Always check output order and enable polarity.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A priority encoder selects the highest-priority asserted input even when several requests arrive together. A separate valid output distinguishes a request for index zero from no request.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Active-high 4-input priority encoder: W3 > W2 > W1 > W0. For W3W2W1W0 = 0110, what is Y1Y0?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: W2 outranks W1, so the winning index is two, encoded 10.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain binary decoders to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A decoder maps a binary address to a selected output line. An enabled active-high decoder asserts exactly one output; its output equations are the address minterms.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Enabled active-high 3-to-8 decoder, address A2A1A0 = 101. Which output index is high?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Binary 101 is decimal five, so Y5 is high.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Output polarity and enable polarity are separate choices. A NAND decoder asserts the selected output at zero; the unselected outputs remain one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Enabled active-low 2-to-4 decoder, address A1A0=10. Y3Y2Y1Y0?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Y2 alone is low; the other three lines are high.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 1011.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A decoder supplies minterm signals. Combining the required minterms realizes a Boolean function; the combining gate must match the decoder output polarity.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Enabled active-high 2-to-4 decoder: implement F(A,B)=A+B, A the MSB. Which lines feed OR?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: OR is one on 01, 10, and 11, so use minterms one, two, three.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us Y1, Y2, Y3.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave combinational building blocks, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A compact truth table can store a smaller function for each selector combination. Reconstruct the full output by choosing the matching case.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A decoder supplies minterm signals. Combining the required minterms realizes a Boolean function; the combining gate must match the decoder output polarity.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You can pause here and try the Combinational building blocks activities. Pick one idea and see whether you can explain it without the notes.

episodes.subject: dl
episodes.title: Timing & arithmetic circuits
episodes.description: Add binary values, follow carries and calculate delay through arithmetic circuits.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, it's Maya. I've got Leo with me for Timing & arithmetic circuits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Learn the rule. Build the circuit. Make it stick.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: add binary values, follow carries and calculate delay through arithmetic circuits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with propagation delay and timing and work our way to signed addition and carry handling.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on propagation delay and timing.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A propagation delay is the time between an input change and the resulting output change. Add delays along dependent paths, not across unrelated parallel paths.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: ns means nanosecond, one billionth of a second.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An input changes at 4 ns and passes through an inverter delayed by 2 ns, then a gate delayed by 3 ns. The final response arrives at 9 ns.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two independent branches of 2 ns and 3 ns are both ready after 3 ns, not 5 ns.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain half adders to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A half adder adds two bits. A full adder adds two bits and a carry-in, producing a low sum bit and a carry-out for the next column.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Half adder means S=A XOR B and C=AB.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Half adder inputs A=1, B=1. Output pair CS?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The total is two, represented by carry one and sum zero.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 10.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A full adder adds two operand bits and an incoming carry. Its sum is odd parity of the three inputs; its carry is one when at least two inputs are one.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Full adder means S=A XOR B XOR Cin; Cout=AB+ACin+BCin.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For A=1,B=0,Cin=1, the total is binary 10. The sum bit is 0 and carry-out is 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Two half adders plus an OR can implement a full adder, but timing depends on the delays of that implementation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A ripple adder connects each column’s carry-out to the next column’s carry-in. High-order results may wait for lower-column carries.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: C0 means initial carry-in. C1: carry after column zero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An eight-bit ripple adder built with one full adder per column uses how many full adders?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Each of the eight bit columns has its own full adder.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 8.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We also need to talk about generate, propagate, and kill.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Generate and propagate signals describe how each operand pair handles an incoming carry. Expanding their equations allows carry look-ahead instead of serial ripple waiting.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Fan-in means number of inputs a gate accepts. Two-input trees may need more levels than unrestricted gates.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Substitute C1=G0+P0C0 into C2=G1+P1C1 to get C2=G1+P1G0+P1P0C0. This uses only G/P and the initial carry.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Count the supplied G/P computation and final sum logic only when the problem includes them.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Carry look-ahead expands carry dependencies into expressions using operand generate/propagate signals and the initial carry. Parallel carry logic removes the serial ripple dependency.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Using Gi=AiBi and Pi=Ai XOR Bi, which recurrence gives carry?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Carry is generated locally or propagated from the preceding column.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose Ci+1 = Gi + PiCi.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Look-ahead timing must include generate/propagate logic, carry generation, and sum generation. Constant logical depth assumes unrestricted fan-in; a limited-input gate network needs additional levels.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Is C0 always zero in an adder?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Block chaining and carry-inclusive addition require a variable carry input.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is No, it may be an external carry input.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: count a look-ahead carry generator.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Count only the explicitly requested carry-generation network. A two-level unshared implementation has one OR per expanded carry and a triangular total of product-term AND gates.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-bit carry generator produces C1 through C4. How many carry outputs?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: There is one generated carry after each of four operand positions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 4.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: With gates of fan-in at most two, parallel carry operations require logarithmic-depth networks. Local generate/propagate logic and final sum logic add constant depth.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Computing all local Pi in parallel changes their depth from constant to linear as n grows?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A fixed-size XOR per bit can run alongside the other bit positions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us No.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: In this implementation, P=A XOR B and G=AB are prepared in parallel. Sum is P XOR Cin, and carry-out is G OR (P AND Cin).

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Inputs ready at zero means timing is measured from their common arrival.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Two-half-adder full adder, all gates 1 ns, inputs ready at zero. Sum-valid time in ns?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The sum traverses first XOR and second XOR.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 2.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack signed addition and carry handling next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Signed addition needs a width and an encoding before the bits can be interpreted. Ones and twos complement differ in how they handle the carry beyond the field.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ones complement means invert the positive magnitude; add an end-around carry.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: In four-bit ones complement, +4 is 0100 and −1 is 1110. Their sum 10010 has an end-around carry: retained 0010 plus 1 gives 0011, or +3.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A twos-complement calculation uses a different negative encoding.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave timing & arithmetic circuits, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A propagation delay is the time between an input change and the resulting output change. Add delays along dependent paths, not across unrelated parallel paths.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Signed addition needs a width and an encoding before the bits can be interpreted. Ones and twos complement differ in how they handle the carry beyond the field.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A useful next step is to revisit signed addition and carry handling with an example of your own. Keep it small enough to check by hand.

episodes.subject: dl
episodes.title: Latches & flip-flops
episodes.description: Predict stored bits using latches, flip-flops and their clock or direct-control inputs.
topics: Convert between SR and T behavior

chapters.title: Convert between SR and T behavior

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome to CSQuest Audio. I'm Maya, here with Leo. This section is called Latches & flip-flops.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Learn the rule. Build the circuit. Make it stick.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: predict stored bits using latches, flip-flops and their clock or direct-control inputs.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with combinational versus sequential circuits and work our way to race-around in level-sensitive toggle storage.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain combinational versus sequential circuits to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Combinational logic depends on current inputs only. Sequential logic also uses stored state, so the same input can produce different next states.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Q means current stored bit. Qnext: bit after an allowed update.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For Qnext=X XOR Q, input X=0 holds the bit and X=1 toggles it. With X=1, current Q=0 becomes 1, while current Q=1 becomes 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The input is identical, but the remembered state differs.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack one-bit storage with feedback next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Cross-coupled inverters have two complementary stable states. Feedback can retain a bit, but the two output nodes do not provide two independent stored bits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: State transition means rule converting current inputs and state to next state.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ideal cross-coupled inverters have settled nodes Q=0 and R. What is R?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Each inverter complements the other node, so R is one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An SR latch stores a bit using feedback. Set requests Q=1, reset requests Q=0, and inactive controls hold the previous state.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: NOR SR latch means active-high S/R; 00 holds, 10 sets, 01 resets, 11 is forbidden.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A NOR latch currently stores Q=1. With S=R=0, it keeps 1; with S=0,R=1, it resets to 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: You cannot infer the held bit from inactive controls alone without knowing its previous state.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A cross-coupled NAND latch uses active-low set and reset controls. State the input polarities explicitly: the hold pair is one-one, and the forbidden pair is zero-zero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: NAND SR latch means active-low controls; 11 holds, 01 sets, 10 resets, 00 is forbidden.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: NAND SR latch, active-low Sbar=0,Rbar=1 held until settled. Q?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The low set input asserts set while reset is inactive.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with latch timing and clock signals. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Latch timing traces must include the stored state. A periodic clock provides high and low intervals separated by rising and falling edges; its frequency is the reciprocal of its period.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: NOR SR latch starts Q=1. Settled input pairs (S,R)=00,01,00,10,00. Final Q?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hold one, reset zero, hold zero, set one, then hold one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An SR storage element sets, resets, or holds a bit. Its characteristic table gives the next state from controls and current state; its excitation table solves the reverse problem of finding controls for a desired transition.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: At a permitted SR update, S=0,R=0,Q=1. Qnext?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hold leaves the stored one unchanged.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A latch is level-sensitive; an edge-triggered flip-flop samples on its specified clock edge.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A storage element’s input rule tells you what bit to store; its trigger tells you when the change is permitted. A latch follows an active level, while a flip-flop samples at an edge.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: D means at an allowed update, Qnext=D.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A rising-edge D flip-flop at Q=0 with D=1 stays at 0 between edges, then captures 1 on the next rising edge.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A high-transparent D latch can follow changes in D throughout the high interval.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on clock levels and active edges.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Level-sensitive storage responds throughout the active clock interval. Edge-triggered storage updates only at its specified transition, even if data changes between transitions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: T means T=0 holds and T=1 toggles.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Negative-edge D flip-flop updates on...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The negative edge is a falling transition.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with Clock 1 to 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: At a permitted update, JK=00 holds, 01 resets, 10 sets, and 11 toggles. Its next-state equation is JQ′ + K′Q, and its excitation table offers input freedom for each desired transition.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: JK means 00 holds, 01 resets, 10 sets, 11 toggles.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Rising-edge JK flip-flop, J=K=1 and Q=0 before its active edge. Qnext?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Toggle complements zero to one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: At a permitted update, T=0 holds and T=1 toggles. The rule Qnext=T XOR Q makes T a compact way to control state changes.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: At a rising-edge T update, T=1,Q=1. Qnext?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Toggle complements the stored one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Now for storage terminology and clock response. What's the key distinction?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Analyze storage from its actual controls and timing behavior. Level sensitivity and edge sensitivity describe how a storage element responds to the clock; different elements can share the same clock waveform.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A cross-coupled NAND pair has only active-low set/reset inputs. Does it inherently wait for a clock edge?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: There is no clock input in the stated circuit.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A conversion makes one kind of storage element behave like another by adding logic before its inputs. Begin with the desired next state for every current-state/input combination.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Characteristic rule means computes next state from inputs and current state.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: When converting available D storage to T behavior, whose excitation rule chooses the physical D input?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The available device needs D equal to the required next state.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with The available D element.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Asynchronous inputs can override clocked behavior.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A PN element has the explicit operations 00 clear, 01 hold, 10 complement, and 11 set. Its characteristic equation is Qnext=PQ′+NQ.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Excitation rule means finds physical inputs needed for a desired transition.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: To make D storage act like T storage, drive D=T XOR Q. For T=0 the input becomes Q and holds state; for T=1 it becomes Q′ and toggles.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Verify both current states rather than testing just one row.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to convert between SR and T behavior. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A conversion must reproduce the target next state using the available device. Current-state feedback lets an SR element toggle or lets a T element set, reset, and hold.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Don’t-care means a choice allowed only on a genuinely unused or unconstrained case.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: SR-to-T conversion S=TQ′,R=TQ; target T=1,current Q=0. Physical S?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: T times complement of Q is 1 times 1, giving one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Asynchronous preset and clear set or reset storage without waiting for a clock edge. Their polarity and priority must be stated.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Preset means force Q to 1. Clear/reset: force Q to 0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For a flip-flop with active-low clear, CLR=0 forces Q=0 even between clock edges. Setting CLR=1 merely releases that control; it does not by itself force Q=1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Simultaneous preset and clear need device-specific rules.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A timing problem combines update opportunities, storage rules, and direct controls. Data must also remain stable around an active edge for a specified capture to be reliable.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Active-low direct control means asserted by a zero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Rising-edge JK starts Q=0, direct controls inactive. Edge pairs (J,K)=00,11,01. Final Q?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hold zero, toggle to one, then reset to zero.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 0.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain master–slave storage to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A master–slave pair uses two storage stages with opposite transparent phases. A directly fed-back level-sensitive toggle loop can instead change repeatedly during a long active interval.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Transparent means the stage can follow its data input. Holding: its output is retained.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: While the clock is high, a high-transparent master can follow D and a low-transparent slave holds. When the clock falls, the master holds and the slave transfers that value.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: In a separate simplified toggle loop, count completed loop delays to determine how many toggles occur.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A level-sensitive feedback circuit can toggle repeatedly while its toggle control and active clock level persist. An edge-triggered update or properly isolated master–slave arrangement avoids repeated changes within one active interval.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: High-master/low-slave D pair means ideal external capture occurs at the falling transition.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Which situation permits repeated toggling (race-around) when the output feeds directly back into a storage element?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Toggle feedback can act again while a level-sensitive circuit remains enabled.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose Level-sensitive JK=11 with a long active clock interval.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave latches & flip-flops, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Combinational logic depends on current inputs only. Sequential logic also uses stored state, so the same input can produce different next states.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A level-sensitive feedback circuit can toggle repeatedly while its toggle control and active clock level persist. An edge-triggered update or properly isolated master–slave arrangement avoids repeated changes within one active interval.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We've covered a lot in latches & flip-flops. You don't have to remember every detail at once; start by trying one of the examples yourself.

episodes.subject: dl
episodes.title: Counters & state sequences
episodes.description: Trace counter states, calculate division ratios and compare ripple and synchronous designs.
topics: Divide a clock frequency by two
Binary up and truncated ripple counters
Budget propagation delay per ripple stage
Trace a custom synchronous T counter

chapters.title: Divide a clock frequency by two
Binary up and truncated ripple counters
Budget propagation delay per ripple stage
Trace a custom synchronous T counter

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, I'm Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Counters & state sequences.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Learn the rule. Build the circuit. Make it stick.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: trace counter states, calculate division ratios and compare ripple and synchronous designs.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with counters and their state sequences and work our way to twisted-ring and Johnson timing counters.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack counters and their state sequences next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A counter stores a binary state and updates it at count events. In a ripple counter, one stage’s output clocks another, so edge polarity and wiring determine the count direction.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Modulus means number of stable states in the repeating cycle.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Two rising-edge toggle stages with Q0 directly clocking Q1 count down: 00→11→10→01→00. Q0 changes first, so a temporary pattern can appear before each settled state.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Frequency division alone does not tell you the direction.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A latch is level-sensitive; an edge-triggered flip-flop samples on its specified clock edge.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Now for divide a clock frequency by two. What's the key distinction?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An edge-triggered storage bit configured to toggle on every active input edge completes one output cycle for every two input cycles. Its output frequency is therefore half the input clock frequency.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: T=1, rising-edge element starts Q=0. Q after five active edges?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Five toggles is odd, so the initial zero becomes one.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Cascading two toggle stages gives divide-by-four frequency division. Count direction depends on the active clock edge and which previous-stage signal drives the next clock; state traces must use an explicit bit order.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: External clock 48 MHz, two cascaded ideal dividers. Q1 frequency in MHz?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Divide by 2 twice: 48/4 = twelve MHz.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is 12.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A full n-bit binary down counter visits all values from 2^n-1 to zero and wraps. Interstage clock choices must make each higher bit toggle when the preceding bit rises during a borrow ripple.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Rising-edge three-bit down ripple chain: clock input of Q2 comes from...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Direct preceding Q provides the required rising-edge borrow trigger.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with Q1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to binary up and truncated ripple counters. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A binary up ripple counter toggles higher bits on carries from lower bits. A truncated modulo-M cycle can reset at a decoded terminal pattern so its stable sequence runs from zero through M-1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Falling-edge up ripple chain: when Q0 falls, the next stage...

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The Q0 falling transition is the active clock edge for the next toggle stage.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us Toggles.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Ripple counters need time for dependent stage changes to settle. Reset logic can shorten a binary cycle, and cascaded counters combine division ratios.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Clock-to-output delay means time from an active edge to a stage’s output change.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Modulo-6 and modulo-10 counters cascaded by one-per-cycle pulses. Combined modulus?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Multiply six by ten to get sixty.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 60.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A custom up counter can reload a chosen starting pattern at the first unwanted count. Distinguish states held for a count interval from the terminal pattern that triggers the reload.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four dependent stages at 5 ns each can need 20 ns to settle. Requiring full settling gives at most 50 MHz before adding any other constraints.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A counter that resets on detecting 10 can have ten stable states, 0 through 9.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain realize a modulo-six ripple counter to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Edge-triggered D elements become toggle stages with D=Q complement. A three-bit up ripple chain can be truncated to six stable states by detecting 110 and asserting clear.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: D=Q complement and Q=1 before the active edge. Next Q?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The input is zero, so the edge captures zero.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We end up with 0.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Under the simplified ripple-settling model, an n-stage transition needs n times the stage propagation delay. The next count event must wait at least that long; additional setup or logic constraints are excluded unless stated.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Four-stage ripple counter, each stage 50 ns, ignoring other constraints. Worst-case full settling delay in ns?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Four times fifty ns equals two hundred ns.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: That gives us 200.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A clock-rate limit can be rearranged to find the allowed delay per stage. The number of stages comes from the counter width, not directly from its decimal modulus.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Full binary modulo-1024 counter: number of one-bit stages?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: 1024 equals 2^10, so ten independent stored bits provide the required binary range.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We also need to talk about reload a selected down-count range.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A down counter can return to a chosen upper value by decoding the first unwanted low count and using preset or clear controls. Count only the stable intended range when determining its modulus.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Stable down range 7 through 3 inclusive. Modulus?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The five stable values are seven, six, five, four, three.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is 5.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Synchronous counter elements share a clock edge. Evaluate every next-state equation using the old state before replacing any bit.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Next-state map means a rule giving a successor to each current state.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Common-edge T counter: T0=1,T1=Q0,T2=Q1, current Q2Q1Q0=000. Next state as decimal?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Only T0 is one, so the next vector is 001.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A wired JK counter is analyzed by substituting current-state bits into its J/K equations. The JK characteristic rule then produces each next bit at the common active clock edge.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Reachable cycle means repeating states found from the specified starting state.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: If Pnext=Q and Qnext=P′, current PQ=01 becomes 11: use old Q=1 for Pnext and old P=0 for Qnext. Do not substitute the newly updated P into the second equation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Continue until a state repeats to identify the cycle.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: trace a custom synchronous T counter.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For the defined three-bit state PQR, use TP=R,TQ=P′,TR=Q′. All next bits use the pre-edge state, and trajectories can include both cycles and transient entries.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Transient means a visited state that does not recur in the eventual cycle.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Common-edge T counter: TP=R,TQ=P′,TR=Q′, current PQR=000. Next state as decimal?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Toggle controls are 0,1,1, so next PQR is 011.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 3.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Counter design starts with the desired state transitions and derives the required storage inputs. T or D input equations can implement binary up counting, while the maximum clock rate depends on the register-to-register critical path.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Current Q2Q1Q0=011. For binary up counting, T2 value?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Both lower bits are one, so Q2 must toggle.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The result is 1.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A ring counter recirculates its last bit; a Johnson counter feeds back its complement. The starting state and shift direction determine the sequence.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: One-hot means exactly one stored bit is 1.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ring rule next ABCD=DABC, current ABCD=0010. Next ABCD?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The last D bit is zero; shift C into D to obtain 0001.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack twisted-ring and Johnson timing counters next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A twisted-ring register feeds the complement of its last bit back to its first stage. Initialized to all zeros, n stages visit 2n states; decoding that valid cycle produces one-hot Johnson timing signals.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A four-stage ring initialized to 1000 can cycle 1000→0100→0010→0001→1000. Starting at 0000 would keep shifting zeros, so initialization matters.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A four-stage Johnson counter’s intended cycle has eight phases instead.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave counters & state sequences, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A counter stores a binary state and updates it at count events. In a ripple counter, one stage’s output clocks another, so edge polarity and wiring determine the count direction.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A twisted-ring register feeds the complement of its last bit back to its first stage. Initialized to all zeros, n stages visit 2n states; decoding that valid cycle produces one-hot Johnson timing signals.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Try explaining twisted-ring and Johnson timing counters in your own words. If you get stuck, that chapter is a good place to listen again.
